\chapter{Bigger, Best and How Long}
\label{ch:ta-bigger-best-and-how-long}
\hlchaptermodality{291}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can compare two things with -aiviṭa, say what I like most with ellāvaṟṟaiyumviṭa, and say how long with mūṉṟu mātamāka, -iliruntu … varai and evvaḷavu nēram.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 291: compare two things, name the most, and say how long something has gone on.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{-\ta{ஐவிட} (-aiviṭa)}{-ஐவிட (-aiviṭa)}]{-\ta{ஐவிட} (-aiviṭa) — bigger than, most of all}

\label{lesson:TA-C291-aivita}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}big\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}small\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{periya}, \emph{ciṟiya}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}a lot\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}less\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{niṟaiya}, \emph{kuṟaivu}.) Then say \textquotedblleft{}dampness\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{īram}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: X-\ta{ஐவிட} Y …}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{இந்த} \ta{வீட்டைவிட} \ta{அந்த} \ta{வீடு} \ta{பெரியது}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inta vīṭṭaiviṭa anta vīṭu periyatu.} — \textquotedblleft{}That house is bigger than this house.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Tamil has no \textquotedblleft{}-er\textquotedblright{} on the describing word. It says \textquotedblleft{}leaving this house aside, that house is big\textquotedblright{}: the thing you compare \textbf{with} takes \textbf{-\ta{ஐ}}, then \textbf{\ta{விட}}, the to-form of \textbf{\ta{விடு}}, \textquotedblleft{}to leave\textquotedblright{}, joined on: \textbf{\ta{வீட்டைவிட}}. \textbf{\ta{அந்த}} (\emph{anta}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}) is the \textbf{a-} of \textbf{\ta{அது}} in front of a noun, as \textbf{\ta{இந்த}} is the \textbf{i-}. \textbf{\ta{பெரியது}} (\emph{periyatu}, \textquotedblleft{}a big one; big\textquotedblright{}) is \textbf{\ta{பெரிய}} made into a thing, like \textbf{\ta{நல்லது}}.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{பேருந்தைவிட} \ta{ரயில்} \ta{நல்லது}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pēruntaiviṭa rayil nallatu.} — \textquotedblleft{}The train is better than the bus.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

With an amount, \textbf{\ta{அதிகம்}}, \textquotedblleft{}more, a lot\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ta{குறைவு}}, \textquotedblleft{}less\textquotedblright{}, do the comparing: \textbf{\ta{இங்கே} \ta{விலை} \ta{குறைவு}} (\emph{iṅkē vilai kuṟaivu}, \textquotedblleft{}prices are lower here\textquotedblright{}).

\subsection*{You'll want to know: the most, \ta{எல்லாவற்றையும்விட}}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{எனக்கு} \ta{எல்லாவற்றையும்விட} \ta{தமிழ்} \ta{பிடிக்கும்}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉakku ellāvaṟṟaiyumviṭa tamiḻ piṭikkum.} — \textquotedblleft{}I like Tamil most of all.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textquotedblleft{}Most\textquotedblright{} is \textquotedblleft{}more than everything\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\ta{எல்லாம்}}, \textquotedblleft{}everything\textquotedblright{}, takes \textbf{-\ta{ஐ}} in the shape \textbf{\ta{எல்லாவற்றை}}, then \textbf{-\ta{உம்}}, \textquotedblleft{}all of it\textquotedblright{}, then \textbf{-\ta{விட}}. For people, \textbf{\ta{எல்லோரையும்விட}} (\emph{ellōraiyumviṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}than everyone\textquotedblright{}):

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{அவள்} \ta{எல்லோரையும்விட} \ta{வேகமாக} \ta{ஓடினாள்}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaḷ ellōraiyumviṭa vēkamāka ōṭiṉāḷ.} — \textquotedblleft{}She ran fastest of all.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{வேகமாக}}, \textquotedblleft{}fast\textquotedblright{}, is the \textbf{-\ta{ஆக}} form of \textbf{\ta{வேகமான}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}That house is bigger than this house\textquotedblright{} — \emph{inta vīṭṭaiviṭa anta vīṭu periyatu}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}The train is better than the bus\textquotedblright{} — \emph{pēruntaiviṭa rayil nallatu}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I like Tamil most of all\textquotedblright{} — \emph{eṉakku ellāvaṟṟaiyumviṭa tamiḻ piṭikkum}
  \item two places you know, compared, with -\ta{ஐவிட}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}Than the bus\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{பேருந்தைவிட}}.) Which case does the compared thing take? (\textbf{-\ta{ஐ}.}) \textquotedblleft{}Most of all\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{எல்லாவற்றையும்விட}}.) \textquotedblleft{}Than everyone\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{எல்லோரையும்விட}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மூன்று} \ta{மாதமாக} (mūṉṟu mātamāka)}{மூன்று மாதமாக (mūṉṟu mātamāka)}]{\ta{மூன்று} \ta{மாதமாக} (mūṉṟu mātamāka) — for how long}

\label{lesson:TA-C291-matamaka}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}The train is better than the bus.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{pēruntaiviṭa rayil nallatu}.) Then the words for a month, a year and \textquotedblleft{}until\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{mātam}, \emph{āṇṭu}, \emph{varai}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: -\ta{ஆக} for a span of time}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{நான்} \ta{மூன்று} \ta{மாதமாகத்} \ta{தமிழ்} \ta{படிக்கிறேன்}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāṉ mūṉṟu mātamākat tamiḻ paṭikkiṟēṉ.} — \textquotedblleft{}I have been learning Tamil for three months.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

The span takes \textbf{-\ta{ஆக}}, the \textbf{-\ta{ஆக}} of \textbf{\ta{நன்றாக}}: \textbf{\ta{மூன்று} \ta{மாதமாக}}, \textquotedblleft{}for three months\textquotedblright{}. Tamil keeps the verb in the present, because the learning is still going on; English says \textquotedblleft{}have been\textquotedblright{}. After \textbf{-\ta{ஆக}} the first letter of the next word doubles in writing: \textbf{\ta{மாதமாகத்} \ta{தமிழ்}}.

\textbf{\ta{வருடம்}} (\emph{varuṭam}, \textquotedblleft{}a year\textquotedblright{}), the everyday word beside \textbf{\ta{ஆண்டு}}, works the same: \textbf{\ta{இரண்டு} \ta{வருடமாக}} (\emph{iraṇṭu varuṭamāka}, \textquotedblleft{}for two years\textquotedblright{}).

For a span that is over, the past needs no \textbf{-\ta{ஆக}}: \textbf{\ta{நான்} \ta{இரண்டு} \ta{ஆண்டு} \ta{மதுரையில்} \ta{இருந்தேன்}} (\emph{nāṉ iraṇṭu āṇṭu maturaiyil iruntēṉ}, \textquotedblleft{}I lived in Madurai for two years\textquotedblright{}).

\subsection*{You'll want to know: from … until, and how long}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{காலையிலிருந்து} \ta{மாலை} \ta{வரை} \ta{மழை} \ta{பெய்தது}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kālaiyiliruntu mālai varai maḻai peytatu.} — \textquotedblleft{}It rained from morning until evening.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{காலையிலிருந்து}} (\emph{kālaiyiliruntu}, \textquotedblleft{}from the morning\textquotedblright{}) is \textbf{\ta{காலை}} with \textbf{-\ta{இல்}} and \textbf{-\ta{இருந்து}}, \textquotedblleft{}from\textquotedblright{}, the same \textbf{\ta{இருந்து}} as in \textbf{\ta{இங்கிருந்து}}. \textbf{\ta{வரை}} closes the span.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{எவ்வளவு} \ta{நேரம்} \ta{ஆகும்}?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{evvaḷavu nēram ākum?} — \textquotedblleft{}How long will it take?\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ta{ஒரு} \ta{மணி} \ta{நேரம்} \ta{ஆகும்}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{oru maṇi nēram ākum.} — \textquotedblleft{}It will take an hour.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ta{ஆகும்}} (\emph{ākum}, \textquotedblleft{}it will become, it will take\textquotedblright{}), the \textquotedblleft{}it\textquotedblright{} future of \textbf{\ta{ஆகு}}; \textbf{\ta{மணி} \ta{நேரம்}} is \textquotedblleft{}an hour\textquotedblright{} of time.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I have been learning Tamil for three months\textquotedblright{} — \emph{nāṉ mūṉṟu mātamākat tamiḻ paṭikkiṟēṉ}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}It rained from morning until evening\textquotedblright{} — \emph{kālaiyiliruntu mālai varai maḻai peytatu}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}How long will it take? It will take an hour.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{evvaḷavu nēram ākum? oru maṇi nēram ākum.}
  \item how long you have lived where you live now
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}For three months\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{மூன்று} \ta{மாதமாக}}.) Which tense says \textquotedblleft{}have been learning\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{The present.}) \textquotedblleft{}From morning until evening\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{காலையிலிருந்து} \ta{மாலை} \ta{வரை}}.) \textquotedblleft{}How long will it take?\textquotedblright{} (\textbf{\ta{எவ்வளவு} \ta{நேரம்} \ta{ஆகும்}?})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — comparing and time}

\label{lesson:TA-R291-comparing-and-time}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}The train is better than the bus.\textquotedblright{} Then \textquotedblleft{}for three months\textquotedblright{}. Then read \textbf{\ta{ஈரம்}} aloud. (\emph{īram}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item My town is smaller than Madurai.
  \item I like tea most of all.
  \item I have been learning Tamil for two years.
  \item It rained from morning until evening. My shirt was wet.
  \item two things you have done for a long time, and for how long
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}Bigger than this house\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{இந்த} \ta{வீட்டைவிட} \ta{பெரியது}}.) \textquotedblleft{}Most of all\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{எல்லாவற்றையும்விட}}.) \textquotedblleft{}For two years\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ta{இரண்டு} \ta{வருடமாக}}.) \textquotedblleft{}From … until\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{-\ta{இலிருந்து} … \ta{வரை}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
